sourceReview.locator: Complete practice4 and5 — one multiple of the other and no common factors contrasts
sourceReview.excerpt:
4.  a.  List the first ten multiples of 12

12, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72, 84, 96, 108, 120

b.  List the first ten multiples of 6

6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48, 54, 60

c.  Identify the common multiples of 12 and 6 from your lists.

12, 24, 36, 48, 60

d.  What is the lowest common multiple of 12 and 6?

12

e.  What do you notice? Why does this happen?

The LCM equals 12, one of the original numbers. When one number is a
multiple of the other, the LCM is the larger number.

5.  a.  List the first ten multiples of 7

7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 49, 56, 63, 70

b.  List the first ten multiples of 9

9, 18, 27, 36, 45, 54, 63, 72, 81, 90

c.  Identify the common multiples of 7 and 9 from your lists.

63

d.  What is the lowest common multiple of 7 and 9?

63

e.  What do you notice? Why does this happen?

The LCM equals 7 × 9 = 63. Since 7 and 9 share no common factors (they
are coprime), the LCM is their product.
